findings.desc: Rework adoption sourceCommit was not rebound to immutable static evidence.
Rework adoption required a sourceCommit without proving a truthful source for it.
Rework adoption is consumed from the backend projection but is not produced by the source-preview adoption UI.
The new rework branch lacked malformed-binding and provenance-drift negative tests.
The rework request id is not duplicated in the adoption projection, and source validation differs between paths.
The new trust-boundary predicate lacked an explanatory comment.
A process-global fixture switch could leak a rework projection into another open browser context.
The positive assertion could fail first on iframe path without identifying an overlay-validator rejection.

dispositions.reason: The source-preview UI is deliberately source-only. Accepted rework candidates are produced by the existing candidate-review decision path and projected server-side; this Feed change only consumes that already-authorized projection.

The immutable reviewBindingDigest already binds the exact reworkRequestId and the server decision receipt binds that digest to the exact-user adoption. Duplicating the request id in the adoption projection would expand the cross-repo schema; source-path validation is unchanged by this bounded correction.
